name: Star Cement Ltd
title: Star Cement Ltd - 540575 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Star Cement Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose to INR324 crore (INR1,871/t) and FY26 PAT more than doubled to INR390 crore; FY27 cement volume guided up 10-12%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was about INR1,174 crore vs INR1,052 crore a year ago, with EBITDA excluding exceptional items of INR324 crore vs INR268 crore and PAT of INR147 crore vs INR123 crore. Cement sales rose to 16.18 lakh tonnes from 14.75 lakh tonnes, while clinker sales jumped to 1.15 lakh tonnes from 0.57 lakh tonnes. For FY26, EBITDA was INR955 crore (INR1,738/t) vs INR589 crore (INR1,245/t), and PAT was INR390 crore vs INR169 crore. Management flagged April-May demand softness from state elections, a near-term fuel and packing cost hit of INR250-300 crore in H1 FY27, and a lower subsidy run-rate in FY27.

financial_highlights.value: INR583 crore gross; INR200 crore net (cash and liquid investments about INR383 crore)

segments.name: Northeast cement
segments.commentary: Q4 Northeast sales were about 11.27 lakh tonnes vs 11.02 lakh tonnes a year ago. Management guides Northeast EBITDA at INR1,500-1,700/t over the next 2-3 years, on a full-year basis.

segments.name: Outside Northeast cement
segments.commentary: Q4 sales were 4.91 lakh tonnes vs 3.74 lakh tonnes a year ago, about 31% growth. Management said trade share was about 78% vs 81% a year ago.

segments.name: Clinker
segments.commentary: Q4 clinker sales were 1.15 lakh tonnes vs 0.57 lakh tonnes. FY27 clinker volumes are expected to be flat at about 3.5 lakh tonnes, with the focus on realisation rather than volume.

segments.name: Non-cement (AAC blocks, RMC)
segments.commentary: Q4 non-cement revenue was about INR17 crore and FY26 was about INR43 crore. FY27 target is about INR150 crore at a 7-8% margin to start.

guidance_outlook: FY27 cement volume growth of 10-12% on about 5.3 million tonnes achieved in FY26 (excludes clinker).
FY27 subsidy income expected to fall by INR40-50 crore vs FY26's INR184 crore, to about INR140-150 crore.
Q1 FY27 fuel cost rise of INR0.15-0.20 per GCV for coal, with the impact expected to ease by June; estimated H1 FY27 cost impact of INR250-300 crore from packing and fuel.
Capex of INR600-700 crore in FY27 and about INR1,500 crore in FY28, contingent on approvals expected by October.
Q1 FY27 EBITDA will face pressure; management expects the Northeast EBITDA/t guidance to hold on a full-year average.
capex_capacity: Nimbol (Rajasthan) clinker plant of about 3.3 million tonnes, plus 2-2.5 million tonnes grinding there and 2-2.5 million tonnes grinding in Haryana; the Rajasthan setup totals about 5 million tonnes of cement capacity. Target start about September 2028 to 1H FY29.

Bihar greenfield grinding unit of about 2 million tonnes, expected 1Q-2Q FY29, supplied with clinker from Meghalaya via Silchar rail siding. Bihar FCSC incentive of 150-200% of investment applied for.
Umrangso (Assam) clinker plant and Jorhat grinding unit (about 2 million tonnes, grinding only), to follow over 4-5 years.
Three-project capex total cited at about INR4,800 crore; the investor presentation will carry a year-wise capex split in about a week.
Clinker factor (CC ratio) was 66.2% in Q4, and management estimates the FY26 ratio at 66.6-67.5%.
demand_pricing: April demand was sluggish due to Assam and West Bengal elections; management sees a pickup in May.
Pricing: Northeast up about INR6-7 per bag and outside Northeast (West Bengal, Bihar) up about INR10 per bag vs the March exit.
Premium cement share was 15.1% in Q4; blend mix was 18% OPC and the rest PPC.
Lead distance fell to about 220 km from 229 km a year ago; KKL cost was about INR1.24 per GCV.
Management expects a new mainland entrant to take 3-4 years; it expects price pressure for 1-2 years after entry, then normalisation.
Green share was about 33.8% in Q4; management guides 30-33% for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 volume guidance and the April-May demand trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guides 10-12% cement volume growth on about 5.3 million tonnes. April was sluggish due to elections, with a pickup in May; it will refine the estimate after June.

qa_highlights.question: How much will subsidies fall in FY27, and what is the capex outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidies fall by INR40-50 crore to about INR140-150 crore. Capex is INR600-700 crore in FY27 and about INR1,500 crore in FY28, subject to approvals by October.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost impact of fuel and packing from the West Asia situation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates an H1 FY27 impact of INR250-300 crore, mainly packing and fuel, with prices partly offset by hikes of INR7 in Northeast and INR10 in North Bengal. Q1 EBITDA will be under pressure, with June expected to normalise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt and cash position?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt is INR583 crore and net debt is INR200 crore, implying cash and liquid investments of about INR383 crore. The non-current investment rise reflects liquid bonds with maturities under one year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Rajasthan and Haryana plant breakevens and realisation targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 80-90% utilisation in 3.5-4 years and prices about INR5-10 below the highest-priced seller. It gave no explicit breakeven year and framed the strategy around brand building and dense distribution.

qa_highlights.question: How will new mainland entrants affect Northeast profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Tushar Bhajanka expects significant pressure once they enter, which may last 1-2 years before normalising. He says Star Cement has the highest trade penetration among Northeast players.

risks_watch: Coal rake shortages and diesel cost increases (INR0.15-0.20 per GCV) could pressure Q1-Q2 FY27 margins.
Subsidy income falls by about INR40-50 crore in FY27, which hits per-tonne EBITDA.
Capex timelines for Nimbol, Bihar and Haryana depend on October approvals; management warned of a 1-2 month slip.
Mainland entrants (Shree, Ambuja, JK Lakshmi) may pressure Northeast prices and EBITDA/t after 3-4 years.
QIP is not approved at Board level; it is linked to net debt/EBITDA of about 1.5x.
Trade share fell to 78% from 81%; the non-trade mix is rising.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume targets and long-term plans, but cautious on near-term costs and demand; management was candid about Q1 EBITDA pressure. It was evasive on capex split by project and on mainland competitors' pricing behaviour.

growth.why: FY27 cement volume guided up 10-12% on ~5.3 mn t, backed by pricing gains (NE +INR6-7/bag, outside NE +INR10/bag) and 31% Q4 growth outside Northeast, but April-May demand was soft and H1 FY27 faces a INR250-300 crore fuel/packing cost hit; new capacity (Rajasthan, Bihar, Assam) is 6-16 quarters away.
